## KC3000 PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD

### High-Performance Storage for Desktop and Laptop PCs

Kingston KC3000 PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD delivers next-level performance using the latest Gen 4x4 NVMe controller and 3D TLC NAND. Upgrade the storage and reliability of your system to keep up with demanding workloads and experience better performance with software applications such as 3D rendering and 4K+ content creation. With formidable speeds up to 7,000MB/s read/write, it ensures improved workflow in high-performance desktop and laptop PCs making it ideal for power users who require the fastest speeds on the market.

The compact M.2 2280 design fits seamlessly into motherboards and gives greater flexibility where high-power users appreciate responsiveness and superior loading times.

Full capacities available from 512GB–4096GB to meet your data storage requirements.

What is the difference between M.2 SATA and M.2 PCIe? 

M.2 is the physical form factor. SATA and PCIe refer to the storage interface, the primary difference is performance and the protocol (language) spoken by the M.2 SSD (e.g., PCIe, SATA).

The M.2 spec was designed to accommodate both a SATA and PCIe interface for SSDs. M.2 SATA SSDs will use the same controller currently on typical 2.5-inch SATA SSDs. M.2 PCIe SSDs will use a controller specifically designed to support the PCIe protocol. Although each M.2 SSD can only support one protocol (e.g., PCIe, SATA), some systems may have M.2 sockets that support both PCIe and SATA. Please check your system's user manual to confirm.

Compare Kingston Fury Renegade SFYRD/2000G and Kingston KC3000 SKC3000D/2048G

Comparing Kingston Fury Renegade SFYRD/2000G and Kingston KC3000 SKC3000D/2048G, it can be noted that both drives feature a PCIe 4.0 interface and similar write speeds (7000 MB/s), however, the KC3000 offers slightly larger capacity at 2048 GB compared to Fury Renegade's 2000 GB. Both devices use the Phison E18 controller and have a 5-year warranty, but the KC3000 supports TRIM and has a higher endurance of 1600 TB compared to 2000 TB of the Fury Renegade. While the Fury Renegade is equipped with a graphene heat spreader for cooling, the KC3000 also has efficient thermal regulation preventing overheating.
